creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A window somebody asks for claims a fresh workspace on every attached machine (`a_2IZ5TL6DQ`: "No `--daemon` flag was added"). With two machines attached that is a new shell on the laptop and a new ssh shell on the devenv, and a person who wanted a laptop window closes the devenv one. There is no way to open a window onto a tab that already exists, and `muster window reopen` takes the most recently written free arrangement rather than a named one.

What it took on 2026-09-08 to get one window on a laptop tab and one on a devenv tab from one home, after a full quit:

1. `open -a Muster`, which took the most recent arrangement, the laptop one.
2. `muster window reopen`, which took the other arrangement. It also pointed at the laptop tab, so both windows opened onto it and raced for its terminal.
3. `muster tab new --daemon devenv --socket <second>`, to give the second window a devenv tab to show.
4. `muster pane reattach --pane <laptop pane> --socket <first>`, because the second window's takeover had left the first window dark.

Earlier the same day, bringing back a laptop window whose arrangement had drifted onto a devenv tab meant editing `showing` in `state/windows/window-2.toml` by hand before `reopen`.

## Directions

- `muster window new --daemon <id>`: a fresh window with a workspace on that machine only. `pane new` and `tab new` already take the flag with this meaning.
- `muster window new --tab <t>`: a window opened onto an existing tab, which moves into it. Depends on a tab belonging to one window (the card on two windows sharing one tab list).
- `muster window reopen <name>` and a listing of closed windows, which `a_2KAFWbZBa` already asks for.

## Validating a fix

- `muster window new --daemon local` opens a window with one tab, on the laptop, and asks nothing of the devenv.
- After a quit, two `reopen`s by name bring each window back onto its own tabs with no bridge refused.
title: 🧭 muster window new cannot say which machine or which tab the window is for
